title: Israel partially reopens the Rafah crossing between Gaza and Egypt for people
body:
On Sunday 1 February 2026, Israel partially reopened the Rafah crossing between Gaza and Egypt, AFP reported. Access was limited to people rather than goods. The crossing had been closed since Israeli forces took control of it in May 2024, apart from a brief, limited reopening in early 2025. COGAT, the Israeli defence ministry body, said the crossing was opened for the limited passage of residents only and described it as an initial pilot phase.

Israel had said it would not reopen the crossing until the remains of Ran Gvili, the last Israeli hostage held in Gaza, were returned. His remains were recovered days earlier and he was buried in Israel on Wednesday, and COGAT announced the reopening two days later. Entry and exit required prior Israeli security clearance and coordination with Egypt, under the supervision of an EU mission. A Gaza health ministry official said about 200 patients were waiting to leave, and a Palestinian official said around 40 people affiliated with the Palestinian Authority reached the Egyptian side to enter Gaza and begin work.

The 15-member National Committee for the Administration of Gaza, led by Ali Shaath and supervised by the Board of Peace chaired by US President Donald Trump, was meant to run day-to-day affairs for Gaza's 2.2 million residents, but was not expected to enter that day. AFP said Gaza's civil defence agency reported dozens killed in Israeli attacks on Saturday, which the Israeli military said were retaliation for truce violations. Israeli forces held more than half of Gaza behind the Yellow Line set under the ceasefire that took effect on 10 October 2025.
